$comment: Save-compatibility manifest (issue #766, save-overhaul C4). Tracks every save-format baseline this build is declared to keep loadable through explicit migrations, plus the tracked fixtures proving it. Never hand-edit a fixture's sha256 after it has been recorded here -- see tools/save_compat_audit.py (--add-baseline registers a fixture's checksum/summary together).
frozenDtoFingerprintOf: src/World/Save/Compat/SessionV90.hs, plus every leaf DTO its frozen types embed, transitively resolved wherever actually defined (World.Save.Component.Page/.Entities/.Session/.WorldGen)
frozenDtoFingerprintComment: sha256 over every frozen `data ... deriving (...)` block's field list (whitespace-normalized) in SessionV90.hs, PLUS (round-16 review) every leaf DTO type those blocks embed (WorldGenParamsDTO and its whole nested worldgen config/state tree, WorldEditDTO, GroundItemsDTO/ItemInstanceDTO, BuildingInstanceDTO, UnitInstanceDTO, etc.), transitively resolved wherever each is actually defined -- SessionV90.hs's own blocks alone said nothing about a field reordered on one of those EMBEDDED types, even though the real B1 wire bytes for it would silently change. See tools/save_compat_audit.py's frozen_dto_fingerprint()/_transitive_dto_blocks(). Changes only when a field is added/removed/reordered anywhere in this transitive closure, never on a comment-only edit. Recompute with: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); from save_compat_audit import frozen_dto_fingerprint; print(frozen_dto_fingerprint())". Last updated deliberately by issue #1092: WorldPageSaveV90.wp90Identity was repointed from WorldIdentityDTO to the newly-frozen WorldIdentityDTOv1, which carries the IDENTICAL two fields (name, optional gloss) the old type did -- a rename of the frozen shape, not a field added/removed/reordered, so every tracked v90 fixture's bytes are unchanged (the unsuffixed name now belongs to the current world-pages v3 identity, which additionally carries language provenance). Same pattern #911 used when it froze WorldGenParamsDTOv1. Last updated deliberately by issue #1233: BuildingSnapshotV90.bsn90Instances, UnitSnapshotV90.usn90Instances and WorldPageSaveV90.wp90GroundItems were repointed from BuildingInstanceDTO/UnitInstanceDTO/GroundItemsDTO to the newly-frozen BuildingInstanceDTOv1/UnitInstanceDTOv1/GroundItemsDTOv1, which carry the IDENTICAL fields those types carried before #1233 appended ItemInstance's external bulk and optional internal storage capacities -- a rename of the frozen shapes, not a field added/removed/reordered within them, so every tracked v90 fixture's bytes are unchanged (the unsuffixed names now belong to the current buildings v2 / units v2 / world-activity v3 shapes, which additionally carry those physical values). Exactly the #1092 pattern one row up. Last updated deliberately by issue #1217: WorldPageSaveV90.wp90UnitSimStates was repointed from UnitSimStateDTO to the newly-frozen UnitSimStateDTOv1, which carries the IDENTICAL fields that type carried before #1217 added the per-request hazard policy to its embedded move target -- a rename of the frozen shape, not a field added/removed/reordered within it, so every tracked v90 fixture's bytes are unchanged (the unsuffixed name now belongs to the current unit-sim v3 shape, whose MoveTargetDTO additionally carries MoveHazardPolicy). Exactly the #1092 / #1233 pattern above. Last updated deliberately by issue #1854: three of WorldPageSaveV90's fields were repointed at newly-frozen shapes that carry the IDENTICAL layout they carried before #1854 re-keyed the live types -- wp90FloraHarvests from the live FloraHarvests alias (now HashMap FloraInstanceId Float) to FloraHarvestsDTOv1 (the tile-keyed HashMap (Int,Int) Float those payloads were written with), wp90ChopDesignations from ChopDesignationDTO (which gained the designated plant's own tile) to ChopDesignationDTOv1 (the bare surface z), and wp90Edits from WorldEditDTO to WorldEditDTOv1 (the eleven-constructor sum, before WePlaceFloraWithIdD was appended). The v90 wire BYTES are unchanged in every case -- each is a rename of the frozen shape, not a field added/removed/reordered within it, exactly the #1092 / #1233 pattern two rows up. The fingerprint moves because it hashes the frozen types' field LISTS, and those field lists now name the frozen types rather than the live ones -- which is the whole point: before #1854 they followed a live alias, so re-keying it would silently have rewritten every shipped v1/v2/v3 and v90 payload's decoding. Last updated deliberately by issue #1844: WorldPageSaveV90.wp90ConstructDesignations was repointed from ConstructDesignationDTO to the newly-frozen ConstructDesignationDTOv1, which carries the IDENTICAL five fields that type carried before #1844 replaced the bare cdMaterialsPaid boolean with an attempt identity and a material receipt -- a rename of the frozen shape, not a field added/removed/reordered within it, so every tracked v90 fixture's bytes are unchanged (the unsuffixed name now belongs to the current world-activity v5 shape, which additionally carries those two). Exactly the #1092 / #1233 / #1217 / #1854 pattern above.
envelopeFramingFingerprintOf: src/World/Save/Envelope/Codec.hs + the wire-relevant bindings in src/World/Save/Envelope/Types.hs (ComponentId/ComponentDescriptor/EnvelopeManifest/envelopeMagic/fnv1a64/encodeW32/decodeW32/encodeW64/decodeW64)
envelopeFramingFingerprintComment: round-15 review: envelopeFramingVersion alone is just an integer someone has to remember to bump -- this sha256 (whitespace-normalized, comment-insensitive, same technique as frozenDtoFingerprint) catches an ACTUAL byte-layout change (header/manifest/checksum framing) shipping with envelopeFramingVersion left untouched, which would otherwise be a new wire format with no format epoch. See tools/save_compat_audit.py's envelope_framing_fingerprint(). Issue #1416 added ONE narrow further exception on top of that comment/whitespace normalization: a locally declared LANGUAGE extension whose effective state Codec.hs ALREADY INHERITS from synarchy.cabal's `common lang` stanza is dropped before hashing, so adding or removing such a declaration -- PR #1001 deleted an already-inherited UnicodeSyntax -- no longer moves this value; that edit cannot change the module's effective extension set, its behavior, or the bytes it writes. Only the module HEADER's pragma run is normalized, and only as far as can be established WITHOUT modelling GHC's extension-implication graph. A leading INERT PREFIX drops declarations of either polarity while the state is provably still the inherited one (which is what makes a lone {-# LANGUAGE NoImplicitPrelude #-} a no-op); past it, every remaining declaration must be in POSITIVE form with no extension named twice. Such a header is a plain set of enables layered on a state that already contains each inherited extension's implied closure. The moment a header turns something off -- directly, or by re-enabling after a disable (NoTypeFamilies, TypeFamilyDependencies, where the second reinstates the TypeFamilies the first removed) -- it is kept verbatim instead, as is pragma-SHAPED ordinary source such as a string literal the codec itself writes. One case is knowingly given up to that boundary as a decided trade-off (owner, 2026-08-19): an inherited NEGATIVE re-declared PAST the prefix (Strict, NoImplicitPrelude) leaves the effective set unchanged and is still retained, because proving that needs the same implication table. The cost is one explicable fingerprint move; the other direction hides a real change. It is NOT a blanket exclusion of LANGUAGE pragmas, because a false negative here is the expensive direction: an extension the module does not inherit (its own Strict) and one whose local declaration REVERSES an inherited default (ImplicitPrelude against common lang's NoImplicitPrelude) are both effective and both still move it, and the inherited set is read live from the cabal stanza rather than hard-coded so it cannot drift into covering an extension that has since become effective. Nothing else is excluded -- imports, the module header and export list, OPTIONS_GHC and every other block pragma, and all the code itself still move this fingerprint. A moved fingerprint is not by itself proof the wire format changed, so it does not by itself call for an envelopeFramingVersion bump. Recompute with: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); from save_compat_audit import envelope_framing_fingerprint; print(envelope_framing_fingerprint())"

baselines.description: The #760-era shape (issue #766 requirement 3: 'the independently split Haskell components from #760', round-7 review): Haskell persistence ALREADY split into the modern per-component registry (core-session/texture-palette/world-pages/world-edits/world-activity/buildings/units/unit-sim/craft-bills/power-nodes -- already decodable at their historical input versions via the SAME ccInputVers dispatch the modern path uses), but Lua state still the single opaque "lua-state" blob map predating #761's versioned Lua components. This window was previously (incorrectly) treated as 'never declared, no removal needed' in retiredBaselines -- but issue #766 requirement 3 explicitly lists it as history THIS epic must support, regardless of whether a manifest existed to declare it at the time (the manifest is what #766 itself creates). World.Save.Envelope.decodeB2SessionEnvelope recognizes an envelope shaped EXACTLY {metadata, core-session, texture-palette, world-pages, world-edits, world-activity, buildings, units, unit-sim, craft-bills, power-nodes, lua-state} (every descriptor required, mirroring the B1 fallback's exact-shape precision), reassembles every Haskell component through World.Save.Component.assembleSnapshot UNCHANGED, then handles "lua-state" the SAME way migrateSessionV90 already handles B1's own legacy Lua blob: an EMPTY payload migrates cleanly (defaulting current Lua modules via the engine's existing isMigratingLegacyBaseline mechanism), a NON-EMPTY one is refused (the pre-#761 Lua deserializer that could interpret it was removed).
baselines.migratedBy: World.Save.Envelope.decodeB2SessionEnvelope

fixtures.provenance: Generated through the real codec (round-10 review: the prior fixture wrongly encoded unit-sim/craft-bills/power-nodes at CURRENT v2, a hybrid shape #760 never actually wrote): c3-typed-reference-v1-minimal's fixture was decoded via the RAW envelope codec (World.Save.Envelope.Codec.decodeEnvelope, not the high-level decodeSessionEnvelope) to recover its REAL component descriptors and payload bytes AS-STORED -- including unit-sim/craft-bills/power-nodes genuinely encoded at their historical v1 (bare-id) shape, exactly as a real #760 writer produced them, since c3's own fixture already carries those exact v1 bytes verbatim (CraftBillDTOv1/PowerNodeDTOv1/PageSimDTOv1's wire encoding is byte-identical to their v2 counterparts -- SamePageRef is a transparent newtype -- so only the DESCRIPTOR's version number actually needed to change, not the payload bytes) -- then every OTHER Haskell component's descriptor/payload was carried over verbatim (metadata, core-session, texture-palette, world-pages, world-edits, world-activity, buildings, units, all single-version so v1 is already current), the two modern lua.unit_ai/lua.building_spawn components were dropped, and a single, required 'lua-state' v1 component was added -- ROUND-18 REVIEW: its payload is the REAL cereal-encoded EMPTY 'HashMap Text Text' (the documented pre-#761 sdLuaModules/snapLuaModules shape -- 8 bytes, a Word64 zero length-prefix), not a hand-inserted zero-byte BS.empty as prior rounds wrongly used (a genuine #760 writer's cereal encoder never produces a literal zero-byte payload for an empty map) -- assembled via World.Save.Envelope.Codec.encodeEnvelope directly (not encodeSessionSnapshot, which always writes the modern 'lua.'-prefixed component names, nor encodeComponentSpecs, which always writes every Haskell component at its CURRENT version). The decoded canonical VALUES are unchanged from the prior fixture (migrateCraftBillDTOv1/migratePowerNodesDTOv1/migrateUnitSimDTOv1 only add the SamePageRef wrapper, not a value change; the lua-state payload's own 8 bytes never surface in the canonical summary), so expectedCanonicalSummary needed no content changes -- only this fixture's own bytes (8 bytes larger) and this baseline's declared component versions did.

Issue #764 (save-overhaul C3) then added a v1->v3 reference-typing migration on TOP of that same Lua contract (wrapUnitState/addOwnerToAiState etc. in scripts/unit_ai_save_refs.lua). This baseline's tracked fixtures below are REAL v1-shaped payloads (bare-number reference fields, no __owner) for both modules, encoded through the genuine scripts/lib/data_codec.lua M.encode via a real HsLua VM (not a hand-rolled reimplementation of the wire format, and not re-synthesized inline the way every OTHER Lua persistence test in this suite does) -- see Test.Headless.Lua.SaveModules's "tracked v1 fixtures from disk" describe block, which reads these exact bytes off disk and runs them through the real saveModules.prepareLoad/applyAll path, asserting the canonical unwrapped result these fixtures' .expected.json files record. The version recorded below (1) is deliberately the OLDEST accepted input version, not the current one (3) -- mirroring the c3-raw-reference-v1 baseline's convention -- since proving the oldest migration still works is this manifest's whole point; the current v1/v2/v3 contract itself remains exercised by every other 'Lua persistence components' test.

baselines.description: Position hold after a completed player move order (issue #1216, SURV-4): lua.unit_ai became v6, adding aiState[uid].holdAnchor -- the destination a COMPLETED player move order leaves the unit standing on (scripts/unit_ai_hold.lua's hold_position candidate, scored at unit_ai_combat.lua's own FOLLOW_COMMAND_UTILITY so the #306 interrupt ladder is reused rather than restated). This baseline tracks a REAL current-format session written by the live engine at lua.unit_ai v6, whose acolyte was given a real player move order through unitAi.commandMove and is HOLDING the commanded tile at save time -- the anchor was written by the live maintainTask arrival branch, not staged, so the new shape has its own compatibility coverage rather than a version number with nothing behind it. The order names the tile the unit already stands on, which is the shortest completion the real verb has: a longer leg is not what a persistence fixture measures, and seed 42 / size 16 puts open lake around the spawn (the terrain every earlier baseline shares), so a distant target would only ever have stall-timed-out. Proving a real walk holds its destination -- and returns to the anchor after a survival interrupt -- is tools/position_hold_probe.py's job. v1-v5 payloads stay tracked by the b3/c3/d1/e1/f1/g1/h1/i1/j1/k1/l1/m1/n1/o1 baselines above and decode with holdAnchor absent, which is exactly right: those sessions had no hold to record.

baselines.description: Ground-sourced autonomous repair targets (issue #1737, completing #302's own-inventory -> ground -> technomule ladder): lua.unit_ai became v7, adding repairJob.fromGround and the page-local repairJob.groundGid -- durable provenance, because a save can land anywhere between the pickup and the repair and only the job itself can then say that the instance in a worker's inventory owes a DROP on the ground rather than a hand-back to a mule. This baseline tracks a REAL current-format session written by the live engine at lua.unit_ai v7, whose acolyte holds an IN-FLIGHT ground-sourced repair job its OWN autonomous scoring claimed over a degraded axe_steel item.spawnGround left 12 tiles away, still in its fetch_ground phase -- so the new shape has its own compatibility coverage rather than a version number with nothing behind it, and the gid half of it is exercised while it still names something. groundGid rides the wire as a typed ground_item reference (scripts/unit_ai_ref_schema.lua), so the integrity graph checks it against the owning unit's page like every other per-page id. The furnace is really built (materials delivered, then addBuildProgress) because repairUtility refuses to score a job with no reachable station for its axis, and the spawn-seeded find_water goal is retired first because its search utility otherwise out-competes a repair a dozen tiles away. v1-v6 payloads stay tracked by the b3/c3/d1/e1/f1/g1/h1/i1/j1/k1/l1/m1/n1/o1/p1 baselines above and decode with both fields absent, which is exactly right: those sessions had no ground rung to record.

baselines.description: The #1845 shape (lua.unit_ai v9): a constructJob carries the BuildingId its own stake returned, held between the queued spawn and the completion that retires the job. building.spawn returns on QUEUED while the completion removes the designation on a different queue, so the job holds that id to know whether its OWN stake landed rather than whether something that merely looks like it is standing at the tile -- designation admission does not check building occupancy, so a stranger really can be. The job here is inside that window: a real designation at (5,5), and the real BuildingId a real building.spawn returned, which has not landed at that anchor. So the field goes through unit_ai_save_refs' typed-reference wrap and the production codec as a resolvable building edge, rather than being hand-built. Two things the fixture is shaped around, both correct behaviour that would otherwise leave it with nothing to carry: a job whose stake IS standing at its anchor completes on the next tick from any distance, and an acolyte within construct scan range of a designation it cannot stake cancels it -- hence the mid-window job and the unit spawned 160 tiles away. The transient staking clock beside the id is stripped at snapshot, which the same payload proves by its absence. A v1-v8 payload has the field ABSENT, which is the correct v9 value: such a job resumes as not-yet-staked and re-stakes, and the engine's own occupancy refusal is what stops it double-building.
